sources.supports: Every write validates its identifiers, an entry identifier through the UUID validator, places them as the path segments of the matching endpoint and forwards the JSON payload unchanged. The replies are parsed advisorily against PlanSchema, PlanEntrySchema or RunSchema.

AddPlanPayloadSchema requires name and accepts description, milestone_id, start_on, due_on, refs and an entries array. An entry carries suite_id, name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids, a runs array, dynamic_filters, start_on, due_on and refs; a nested run carries name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids and refs. AddPlanEntryPayloadSchema matches an entry. UpdatePlanEntryPayloadSchema omits config_ids and runs, which TestRail does not accept, and suite_id, which the endpoint's request body does not carry. AddRunToPlanEntryPayloadSchema requires config_ids and omits name, which TestRail derives from the configuration; UpdateRunInPlanEntryPayloadSchema omits both. No payload is parsed by the public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.
zObject uses passthrough, so the declared payload types admit unknown properties; the MCP boundary must reject them separately.

add_plan requires name and accepts description, milestone_id, start_on, due_on and an entries array. add_plan_entry takes suite_id, required for projects with multiple suites or baseline support, plus name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids, refs, start_on, due_on and runs; its top-level config_ids lists the combined configurations for the entry's runs, and every configuration a nested run names must appear in it, each run naming one full combination with one configuration per group. The reference states that config_ids and runs are not supported on update_plan_entry. add_run_to_plan_entry requires config_ids and takes description, assignedto_id, start_on, due_on, include_all, case_ids and refs; TestRail derives the run's name from its configuration.

input_policy.notes: Strictness is an MCP boundary requirement at every depth of the payload, and here it is the only enforcement: the driver forwards this payload without parsing it. The entry and nested-run objects are held to the same rule as the plan itself, so a field misplaced one level up or down is refused rather than silently sent.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the created plan, entries included, returned as the driver received it; entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown field of the plan itself, including one that belongs to an entry rather than the plan.
Reject an unknown field of an entry, including one that belongs to the plan rather than the entry.
Reject an unknown field of a nested run, including one that belongs to the entry rather than the run.

Reject a nested run's name. TestRail's reference names assignedto_id, include_all and case_ids as the fields a nested run may override, and its runs example carries no name; the driver's payload schemas say why, recording that TestRail derives a nested run's name from its configuration combination, which is also why the standalone add_run_to_plan_entry payload omits the field. Accepting it here would report a naming that never took effect.

parameters.semantics: A selection filter in the form the TestRail interface produces: a mode, which the payload declares as a string rather than a number, and a filters map whose keys name a field such as cases:priority_id. The values are forwarded as given, since TestRail's own examples vary their shape from one field to the next. The object carries nothing beyond those two fields, and an extra one is refused.
